appraisal_events.evidence: Observé à son insu, le baron « bedonnant, vieilli par le plein jour, grisonnant » relâche « cette vitalité factice » ; le narrateur note qu'il « eût été fâché s'il avait pu se savoir regardé », car « cet homme, qui se piquait si fort de virilité, à qui tout le monde semblait odieusement efféminé » lui faisait penser « à une femme ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's unseen surveillance strips Charlus of the willed self-presentation on which his prestige rests, and the closing revelation contradicts precisely the virility he prides himself on; the diminishment is qualified but not cancelled by the narrator's tenderness toward the sculptural beauty and the 'aménité, bonté' the unguarded face reveals.

appraisal_events.evidence: Jupien, « perdant aussitôt l'air humble et bon que je lui avais toujours connu », pose « avec une impertinence grotesque son poing sur la hanche », fait « saillir son derrière » ; « Je ne savais pas qu'il pût avoir l'air si antipathique », bien que le narrateur admette ignorer aussi « qu'il fût capable de tenir à l'improviste sa partie ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The mute pantomime with Charlus locally lowers Jupien: the narrator explicitly withdraws the humble goodness he had always credited him with and calls the display grotesque and antipathetic, while conceding an unsuspected virtuosity in the performance.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus is locally lowered by an exposure he did not authorize and by the fat, 'négligent, ridicule' posturing of the courtyard scene, though the narrator's sympathy for his revealed gentleness keeps the fall moderate.
He loses control over his own legibility: watched without knowing it, his face betrays what his whole social manner is built to conceal.
The narrator revises his standing appraisal of Jupien downward, replacing 'humble et bon' with grotesque impertinence and antipathy.
The narrator holds the hidden vantage and announces the discovery as 'si importante en elle-même', gaining local authority as the discerning observer who sees what the participants cannot.

ambiguities: The narrator's treatment of the unguarded Charlus fuses exposure with genuine tenderness — the marble profile, the 'finesse plus spiritualisée, plus douce', the regret that he masks his kindness — so the passage is readable as sympathetic elevation as well as unmasking; it is scored as mixed-polarity diminishment because the revelation lands on the one attribute Charlus stakes his standing on.

The Charlus-Jupien meeting stages a mutual recognition ('en harmonie', 'l'entente se fait d'elle-même') that the botanical frame presents as the improbable insect finally reaching the waiting flower, which could read as a positive attainment; the unit stops before any realized intimacy and its dominant register is ridicule, so it is not scored as consummation or renewal.
